qs.q: A 33-year-old woman undergoing evaluation for infertility is found to have bilateral tubal scarring and a history of chronic pelvic pain. A biopsy of her fallopian tube reveals granulomatous endometritis and salpingitis. Which underlying infectious agent should be strongly suspected in this endemic area?
qs.e: Tuberculosis causes granulomatous endometritis, often associated with TB salpingitis and peritonitis, which is common in endemic areas. Gonorrhea and chlamydia typically cause acute or chronic nongranulomatous suppurative inflammation.

qs.q: The diagnosis of chronic endometritis specifically requires the presence of
o: Plasma cells in the endometrial stroma
qs.e: Lymphocytes are normally present in the endometrium and are not diagnostic. Plasma cells are the key diagnostic requirement for chronic endometritis.
